title: Quarterly Priority Synchronizer — Exec Comms Draft (v0.1)
content:
Purpose
- Create a compact "Priority Synchronizer" that turns executive intent into a single-page cascade for teams + an all-staff narrative.
- This is the working draft for the Exec Comms (pre-allstaff) and the short, actionable OKR mapping we hand to managers.

Executive summary (one paragraph)
- We are entering a 12-week execution window where delivering predictable inference economics + reliability is the prime business constraint. The goal of this quarter: 1) Lock a reproducible 20% reduction in per-token cost for high-throughput customers (via batching and quantization profiles), 2) Ensure Dedicated capacity latency SLOs are consistently met at 95th percentile, and 3) Finish v1 of private deployment onboarding checklist + audit automation. This note aligns those asks to a comms narrative and proposes the all-staff run-of-show.

How to use this doc (quick)
- Execs: copy the "Talking Points" for your 6-min update.
- Managers: use the OKR mapping to drop into team weekly standups.
- RD/PMs: review the risk scenarios and pick contingency owners.

Priority Synchronizer (top-level commitments)
- Priority A (Commercial leverage): Reduce per-token cost for high-throughput customers by 20% measured on Redwood Hosted for top 10 workloads. Owner: Arman. Success metric: median unit cost delta <= -20% vs baseline by week 9.
- Priority B (Reliability): Meet Dedicated 95th percentile latency SLO for reserved customers under production load. Owner: Sofia. Success metric: SLO met for >= 95% of windows for 30-day rolling.
- Priority C (Compliance/Private): v1 private onboarding + audit automation shipped to 3 pilot customers. Owner: Diego. Success metric: 3 customer signoffs + automated KMS audit runbook.

OKR rough mapping (manager-facing short-form)
- O: Make inference predictable and economical for production customers (Q2).
  - KR1: 20% reduction in per-token cost (top 10 workloads) — Arman (eng-serving-runtime + optimize)
  - KR2: 95% 95th-pctl latency SLO for Dedicated — Sofia (sre + dedicated)
  - KR3: Private onboarding kit + audit automation for 3 pilots — Diego (private-deployments + security)

All-staff update run-of-show (15 minutes total)
- 0:00–0:02: CEO one-liner (context + north star).
- 0:02–0:06: Product/Value summary — 3 bullets framing Priority A/B/C. (Use talking points below).
- 0:06–0:10: Engineering highlight — short demo or artifact: batching/quantization chart + expected cost delta.
- 0:10–0:13: GTM/customer highlight — 1 pilot success / ask of early customers for feedback.
- 0:13–0:15: Manager asks & where to find the detailed playbooks + slack triage channel.

Exec talking points (copyable, short)
- "This quarter we are focused on making inference predictable at scale: lower unit economics for heavy customers, and fewer latency surprises for Dedicated customers. That combination unlocks faster adoption for product teams who need both scale and reliability."
- "We have three clear priorities: improve economics through smarter serving and model profiles; harden latency and SLOs for reserved workloads; and make private deployment onboardings repeatable and auditable."
- "If you are a manager: you will get a one-page OKR map in your manager thread; pick the two signals your team will own, and sync with your PM/EM by next Friday."

Talking artifacts to surface during all-staff
- Cost delta chart (batching + quantization sim) — slide 4.
- 95th-pctl latency waterfall demo (Dedicated) — short clip, slide 6.
- Private onboarding checklist snapshot + pilot timeline — slide 9.
- Link to the manager one-pager (Confluence) + weekly cadence template.

Manager one-pager (what we hand to managers) — (short template)
- Priority alignment (bullet)
- Concrete team signals to track (2–3 metrics)
- Weekly check: blocker + escalation owner (name + Slack)
- Delivery windows (hard dates)

Risk scenarios & contingency (short)
- Risk: Quantization causes quality regressions for 1 of top 10 workloads. Contingency: rollback profile + canary testing + human-in-loop eval set. Owner: Arman.
- Risk: Dedicated SLOs miss under a network degradation. Contingency: auto-fallback to regional capacity + traffic shaping. Owner: Sofia.
- Risk: Pilot customers on Private delay signoff due to policy reviews. Contingency: expedited compliance docs + one-off support hours. Owner: Diego.

Immediate next steps (this week)
- Draft manager one-pager + publish on Confluence — Leah (due: 2026-02-26).
- Pull cost-sim charts and embed into slide deck — Arman (due: 2026-02-23).
- Produce 60s latency demo clip for all-staff — Sofia (due: 2026-02-24).
- Finalize private onboarding checklist and pilot sequence — Diego (due: 2026-02-28).
- Create #priority-sync Slack channel and invite execs + managers — Leah (due: 2026-02-19) [TODO: still pending].

Open questions / notes-to-self
- Do we want to call the initiative "Priority Synchronizer" publicly? Might be too internal-sounding — options: "Predictable Inference Quarter" or "Inference Resilience Sprint".
- Should managers declare their 2 signals in a shared spreadsheet or in Confluence comments? Spreadsheet easier for rollups, Confluence is canonical. Suggest spreadsheet + link into Confluence.
- Who owns the escalation playbook for cross-region fallback? (SRE + platform-engineering co-owned). Need a clear primary.

Dependencies & cross-team asks (callouts)
- Eng: need model onboarding support for quantization experiments (applied-ml).
- Console: need per-route cost breakdown visible in the manager dashboard (product-console).
- Solutions / CS: prepare 2 pilot customers who can accept early quantized models for cost measurements.

Comms cadence proposed
- Tue: Exec preview + manager one-pager published.
- Wed: Manager sync (30m) to confirm signals.
- Thu: All-staff (15m) with demo and ask.
- Weekly: 30m cross-functional triage for cadence (ops+eng+cs).

Appendix (short snippets managers can copy into standups)
- "This week: we're prioritizing a 20% unit-cost reduction for our heaviest workloads. Watch the ops channel for a cost sim and sign up if you have representative traffic."
- "If you own Dedicated SLAs: confirm your fallback region and a single escalation owner by next Friday."

Persona notes (how to frame for different audiences)
- Engineers: specific metric and rollback story; provide experiments, data, and clear cutoffs.
- Sales/CS: customer-facing wins and pilot availability; include FAQs about model quality changes.
- Execs: risk, timeline, leverage (cost + SLO).

Draft communication timeline (publish-ready)
- Monday (pre-announce email to managers): short memo + manager one-pager link.
- Wednesday (all-staff): 15m presentation + Q&A via Slack post.
- Friday (follow-up): commit board published with owner roster + triage meeting invite.

Checklist before all-staff (hard gates)
- Slide deck: cost charts + latency clip + pilot status (done).
- Manager one-pager (published).
- Slack channel created and seeded with threads (done/pending).
- Exec talking points reviewed by CEO and Head of Product (in progress).

Final notes (draft tone and style guidance)
- Keep the all-staff tone pragmatic and short. Avoid engineering jargon when describing customer impact. Use 3 clear asks for the org (two signals, escalate owner, cross-functional triage slot).
- Primary narrative: "we are turning engineering levers into predictable economic outcomes for customers" — call out customer examples.

[END - rough draft v0.1]
